item.title: Slip-Event Timing and Ice Velocity Vary at Long-Period Ocean Tidal Frequencies at Whillans Ice Plain, West Antarctica
item.description: @article{10.1029/2025JF008770, title = {Slip-{Event} {Timing} and {Ice} {Velocity} {Vary} at {Long}-{Period} {Ocean} {Tidal} {Frequencies} at {Whillans} {Ice} {Plain}, {West} {Antarctica}}, volume = {131}, copyright = {© 2026. The Author(s).}, issn = {2169-9011}, url = {https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1029/2025JF008770}, doi = {10.1029/2025JF008770}, abstract = {Whillans Ice Plain (WIP), a region of West Antarctica flowing into the southern Ross Sea, lurches forward 0.2–0.6 m over 30–60 min once or twice per diurnal ocean tidal cycle. Combining 11 years (2008–2019) of 30 s or better resolution Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) data from past field campaigns is necessary to provide insight into WIP dynamics by connecting individual slip events to decadal velocity trends.
